verdicts.why: Describes the word as naming a whole outline without judgement, which fits 'having an oval body' and the neutral charge.
Shortness as a proportion, not a verdict, matches 'relatively short body' and stays inside the word.
The gloss says 'silver-colored body' but the note says the word 'asserts the metal outright rather than a likeness to it', reading the compound as material rather than colour.

The note's own account ('the same colour softened into resemblance') fits the gloss, but its contrast clause repeats the misreading that *silver-bodied* 'claims the metal itself' when both share the gloss 'silver-colored'.
Slimness reported with elegance fits 'having a slim body' and the positive charge; the contrast with thin-bodied stays inside the word.
Quiet approval of slimness fits the gloss and positive charge; the neighbour comparison is about force, not distribution.
Surface rather than dimension, agreeableness in the texture not a verdict, fits 'having a smooth body' and neutral.
Bulk that can land as a verdict is a plausible negative reading of 'having a thick body' and the note stays inside the word.
Slimness with the compliment drained fits the shared gloss and a neutral charge; contrast with slim-bodied is about force.
Plainest, least formal member of the deciding-power set fits the gloss and the example 'cast the deciding vote'.
Covers both actually determining and having the power to, exactly as the gloss does, and takes no view on outcome; examples fit.
Formal, analytic, deciding power as a held property fits the gloss; 'formal' is a register label.
Formal and tilted toward a standing quality fits 'having the power or quality of deciding'; contrast with determining stays inside the word.
Deciding power shown in use rather than held is a fair reading of the participial form against the same gloss.
Decisive importance coloured as doom fits the gloss and the negative charge; the election-day example fits this sense.
Gravity and a shadow over momentous consequences fits the gloss and a plausible negative charge; the example fits.
Discourteous force that ends debate and action fits 'putting an end to all debate or action' and negative; 'a peremptory decree' fits.
Absolute rather than graded reads 'utterly cast down' directly and the negative charge follows.
Softest word for the despondency, understating what the gloss covers, is a description of force; example fits.
Stress on being brought low from a height fits 'brought low in spirit' and negative.
Force in the fall rather than the level fits the gloss; 'blunter-sounding' is about the word, not its users.
Spirit stood higher before lowering fits 'brought low' and distinguishes it from the level-only words inside the word.
Flatness, spirit gone out of something, mildest of the set fits the gloss and negative; example fits.
Plain unmarked word for low spirits fits 'affected or marked by low spirits' and the negative charge; example fits.
Weight stated flatly without the softening of blue or down fits the gloss and negative; example fits.
Names the loss of spirit as depletion, fits the gloss and negative; example fits.
Informal, brief, level-only reading fits the gloss and negative; the synset examples illustrate this sense.
Informal, wry, pointing at a visible droop fits the gloss and negative; register label is allowed.
Whole bearing lowered, more picture than down, fits the gloss and negative; example fits.
Gentle, sympathetic, despondency seated in the heart fits the gloss and negative; example fits.
Settled climate rather than one blow fits the gloss and negative; examples fit this sense.
Hard-edged melancholy that has set fits the gloss and negative; example fits.
Barest term giving only the level fits the gloss and negative; contrasts stay inside the word.
Clinical, purely negative in shape, only absence of jaundice fits 'not affected by jaundice' and neutral.
Health with energy spilling out fits 'vigorously healthy' and positive; 'a bouncing baby' fits.
Health judged by tone and resilience of tissue fits the gloss and positive; 'firm muscles' fits.
Health read off skin colour as evidence fits 'having the pinkish flush of health' and positive.
Great health of body or mind carried in the constitution fits 'endowed with or exhibiting' and positive.
Excellent condition stated without flourish fits 'in excellent physical condition' and positive; examples fit.
Formal, a little grand, covering vigour regained or never lost tracks 'exhibiting or restored to' exactly; example fits.
Flat baseline verdict on body or mind alike fits the gloss and positive; examples fit.
Approval through appetite, how someone eats rather than how they are, fits 'consuming abundantly and with gusto'; example fits.
Same great health pitched as raw force fits the gloss and positive; contrast with full-blooded stays inside the word.
Health worn as a boast of vitality fits the gloss and positive.
Pink flush placed in the cheeks as a portrait fits 'having the pinkish flush of health' and positive.
Locating the glow and making it fonder fits the gloss and positive.
Unadorned glow standing alone fits the gloss and positive; contrast with rosy-cheeked stays inside the word.
Excellent condition with the ring of a verdict fits the gloss and positive; example fits.
